newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity higher on outage, NW constraints.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity higher on outage, NW constraints.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures regained some of Monday's selloff on Tuesday with support from a generation plant outage in the Southwest and constraints on Northwest spot electricity sales, industry sources said.
The 750 megawatt Four Corners coal-fired plant in Arizona was shut Monday, and was roughly estimated to be down for six days for boiler tube leak repairs.
Also, Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said it was offering no surplus power for Wednesday schedulings. BPA has not offered spot power for sale since late last week.
"The BPA news seems to be giving COB (California Oregon Border futures) a good boost," said one New York based futures broker.
Electricity futures finished sharply lower Monday, ending a strong up trend that dominated last week.

As of 1230 EDT, December COB was trading up 64 cents at $23.45 per megawatt hour (MWh) from trade in a range of $22.75-23.70, while January COB was up 33 cents at $20.85 from trade in a range of $20.85-21.25 per MWh.
December Palo Verde (PV) was trading 60 cents higher at $21.35 after reaching as high as $21.40, while January PV was up 85 cents at $19.60 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1155 EST a total of 101 COB and 14 PV contracts had traded.
COB open interest for Nov 4 fell 21 to 3,813 while PV open interest rose 95 to 1,772, NYMEX said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
